messages:
alex: heads-up — the canary rollout for q4 kernels (model redwood/gpt-small-q4) is showing a sharp throughput drop and an unexplained GPU memory spike on the schedulers. tokens/sec down ~30% on average, some nodes hitting +4GB memory compared to baseline.

infra-bot: [alert] canary-deploy-4392: increased mem usage on pool-q4-sched (3/8 nodes above threshold). see /ops/alerts/4392

maria: concrete numbers? p50/p95/p99 for tokens/sec and GPU mem?

alex: quick snapshot from dashboard: p50 tokens/sec -30%, p95 -45%, p99 ~ -60%. GPU mem on affected nodes increased by ~3.8GB steady during steady-state. Latency p95 increased by ~120ms.

jonathan: curious — did kernel selection flip to the new fused q4-attn kernel or are we falling back frequently?

alex: profiling shows frequent kernel fallback on attention: kernel_selector logged ~18% fallback rate for step kernel -> scalar-attn. That matches a lot of small kernel launches in profiler.

sam: fallback would increase temporary allocs. Could be KV cache fragmentation + repeated alloc/free pattern. Any change to KV eviction policy in this rollout?

alex: no config change to eviction itself. But the new scheduler heuristics (continuous batching) tightened batch packing thresholds; more variance in sequence-length grouped batches. That may interact with kernel selection (some kernels prefer power-of-two blocked dims).

maria: paste from perf trace (condensed):
```
# trace snippet
time_per_token: +1.9x
attention_kernel: fused-q4-attn (wins: 82%, fails: 18%)
fallback_kernel: scalar-attn (allocs: +42k, tmp_mem: +3.2GiB cumul)
KV_cache: live_entries +12% on affected nodes
batch_size_dist: mean_seq_len 312 -> 427 (canary)
```

jonathan: mean sequence length jump explained by recent traffic shift (longer prompts this week) but we didn't account for how q4 kernels scale with seq_len. Fused kernels pre-allocate temporaries proportional to seq_len and head dim for certain codepaths.

sam: so hypothesis: scheduler packs longer sequences more densely -> triggers fused-q4 for some shapes -> when fallback occurs we allocate additional temporaries and don't reuse them effectively -> eviction thrash in KV cache -> net memory pressure and perf drop.

maria: do we have per-kernel memory footprint numbers for q4 fused vs fallback?

alex: quick table from microbench harness:
```
fused-q4-attn: scratch_mem ~ 0.8 * seq_len * B (GiB units scaled)
fallback-scalar-attn: alloc pattern many small buffers totalling ~1.2 * seq_len
```
On long sequences, fallback > fused in peak, but the fragmentation causes the allocator to spike. Also the allocator doesn't return memory quickly which keeps GPU resident high.

jonathan: what's odd is fallback rate should be low; why are we falling back that much? Are we hitting a kernel selection guard (e.g., unsupported sequence length or head dim) or a runtime check failing due to alignment?

alex: logs show alignment warning on ~1% of requests: "kernel shape unsupported: headdim=49" — because some custom models have non-64 head dims. With packing we end up combining sequences from different model variants in the same batch (we allowed cross-model batching as an optimization). Mixed headdims -> more fallback.

sam: cross-model batching + tighter packing = mixing incompatible shapes -> kernel fallback -> alloc thrash. That pipeline change is recent (scheduler config v2.7).

maria: action items proposed: 1) temporarily disable cross-model batching on q4 pool, 2) revert scheduler tight packing threshold for canary nodes, 3) collect detailed GPU heap snapshots, per-kernel mem histograms, and full allocator traces.

alex: Agreed. I'm going to flip cross-model batching OFF for pool-q4-sched now.

infra-bot: command accepted: set scheduler.pool-q4-sched.cross_model_batching=false (canary scope). rolling to 3/8 nodes.

jonathan: also let's add a kernel_selector debug flag that logs the specific reason for fallback (alignment vs unsupported op vs runtime error). That will help avoid blind guesses.

sam: I'll add an allocator metric: gpu.alloc_frag_ratio and gpu.resident_histogram to telemetry for the q4 pool.

maria: can we run a synthetic replay with long-tailed sequences to reproduce? I can spin a load generator with mixed headdims and sequence distribution matching last 72h.

alex: please do. target: reproduce fallback rate >10% and mem spike. If we can repro, we'll try a small patch: 1) prefer avoiding packing incompatible shapes; 2) adjust kernel_selector thresholds to prefer stability over raw perf for canary.

maria: starting job: replay/1768504321-long-tail (uses sequences from prod/long_prompts sample). ETA ~6m.

[~6 minutes later]

maria: replay reproduces. fallback rate 21%, mem spike +3.6GB, throughput -32%. Turning off cross-model batching immediately improves fallback -> 3% and mem back to baseline. Throughput recovers ~+28%.

alex: rolling this to all canary nodes then aborting the broader rollout. Also open a PR to change default: cross-model-batching=false for any pool with q4 kernels until kernel_selector handles mixed head dims.

jonathan: long term we should:
- teach scheduler to partition batches by compatible kernel shapes (head dim, dtype) before packing
- augment model metadata with kernel-friendly shape hints so packing can be shape-aware
- add allocator improvements: slab reuse for temp buffers used by fused q4 kernels

sam: I'll start a telemetry ticket to track "cross_model_batching" impact across pools and add dashboard panel for kernel_fallback_rate per pool.

alex: owners: alex (rollout revert), maria (replay + repro artifact), jonathan (kernel_selector debug), sam (telemetry + allocator metrics). I'll open the rollback ticket and notify SRE oncall.

maria: PR and rollback ticket created: https://git.redwood/infra/rollbacks/5996

alex: thanks team. We'll wait for telemetry to stabilize and reconvene if anything unexpected pops up. :thumbsup:
